sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: This guide takes you from opening the RMNCAH or Vaxx app in DataSuite to a dataset that is ready for analysis. The methodology behind these steps is described in Analysis setup.

sections.heading: Start the app from DataSuite
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] On the DataSuite welcome page choose Open in RMNCAH (see Navigating the DataSuite interface). The app needs a file to work on, so DataSuite asks you to pick one. Accepted types are .xls, .xlsx, .dta and .rds.

Use the Excel workbook from the Data Extractor the first time, and the saved .rds afterwards.

[Vaxx] Open DataSuite, go to the Start page and choose Vaxx. The app opens on the Introduction page, which presents the Countdown immunization coverage and inequalities project in English, French or Portuguese. Use Load Data in the left navigation to begin.

If you launch the app by opening a data file in DataSuite, that file is loaded for you.

sections.heading: Check that the file was read
sections.text:
Open Load Data in the sidebar. When DataSuite hands the file to the app, it is read automatically and a green Upload successful banner names the file. If the page shows an Upload HFD data box instead, choose the file there.

Loading routine data

sections.heading: Accepted files
sections.text:
Format | Notes
.xlsx

,

.xls | A workbook with the required sheets (see

Analysis setup > HMIS data

). Starts the full walkthrough.
.dta | A single, already merged Stata file.
.rds | A dataset saved by this app. It is already validated, so the app opens a summary of the dataset instead of the walkthrough.

Other extensions are refused with "Upload failed: Unsupported file format."

When you upload an Excel or Stata file, the app looks for its saved copy and loads it instead if it exists. This is how work resumes.

[RMNCAH] The saved copy is named after your file with _rmncah.rds added, in the same folder.

When you open the same Excel or Stata file again, the saved _rmncah.rds copy next to it is used instead. Delete that copy if you changed the workbook and want to load it afresh.

[Vaxx] Files of up to 2 GB are accepted. The saved copy is named name_vaccine.rds. In a desktop session the copy sits next to your file; from a browser it is kept in a fixed local folder.

If a saved .rds copy cannot be read, the app falls back to the original Excel or Stata file automatically.

sections.heading: Two ways through Load Data
sections.text:
- A resumed .rds file was already validated. The wizard is replaced by a Ready for analysis page with one row per step (for example 15 of 15 fields set, Using the built-in shapefile) and an Edit link that reopens any step. Continue to analysis takes you to Reporting Rate.
- A new Excel or Stata file goes through the walkthrough below. The wizard has a step rail. Steps unlock in order: a step opens only after you press Continue (or Skip to) on the previous one, and a step marked required must be complete before the next one opens. Steps marked optional can be skipped.

sections.heading: Upload Data
sections.text:
Drop or browse for your file in the Dataset card ("Browse or Drop..."). The card shows the loaded file. Download Master Dataset saves the merged dataset as a .dta file (master_dataset.dta). Clearing the file also clears everything derived from it.

The card Additional reference data (optional) lets you replace the built-in country reference sets with your own .dta files:

[RMNCAH] Upload UN Estimates data, Upload WUENIC estimates and Upload UN Mortality estimates. Restore default returns to the built-in data.

[Vaxx] Your own UN estimates and WUENIC estimates.

sections.heading: Data Quality
sections.text:
The checks run automatically on the loaded sheets. A banner reads either All checks passed, no blocking issues found or Some checks found issues that need fixing before you can continue. The page lists blocking checks (they must pass before Continue works), informational checks (they do not block) and mapping checks (region name mismatches, fixed in the mapping steps).

What each check tests: Analysis setup > Checks on the uploaded data.

Fix blocking problems in the workbook (the source file) and load it again.

sections.heading: Survey Files (optional)
sections.text: Upload up to five .dta files in the Survey data folder card, one at a time: National data, Regional data, Area data, Maternal education data and Wealth index quintile data. What they are used for, and what happens without them: Analysis setup > Survey files and shapefile. A file that cannot be read shows Upload failed with the reason.

sections.heading: National Rates
sections.text:
Enter or confirm the survey values used to derive denominators. Every field is required and Continue stays disabled while Required fields remaining is shown.

- Survey reference: Recent Survey Year and Survey Data Start Year.

[RMNCAH] - Maternal and newborn: ANC1, ANC4, Institutional Delivery, C-Section and Low Birth Weight coverage, and Pregnancy Loss, Twin Births, Stillbirth, Neonatal Mortality and Post-Neonatal Mortality.
- Immunization: BCG, Penta1, Penta3 and Measles 1 coverage.

National rates for denominator calculation

[Vaxx] - Survey coverage for ANC1, institutional delivery, BCG, Penta1, Penta3, OPV1, OPV3 and Measles 1.
- National rates for pregnancy loss, twin births, stillbirth, neonatal mortality and post-neonatal mortality.

If you uploaded a national survey file, the values are pre-filled and a banner says so. Check them. What each value means, its unit and allowed range (percentages or proportions), and how to choose the survey years: Analysis setup > National parameters.

sections.heading: Shapefile (optional)
sections.text: The app uses a built-in (standard) shapefile for the country by default (Analysis setup > Survey files and shapefile). To use your own, upload the .shp, .dbf, .shx and .prj files, pick the column that holds the region (admin-1) names and press Use this shapefile.

sections.heading: Map Survey and Map Shapefile
sections.text: When you uploaded survey files or a custom shapefile and their region names differ from your dataset, match them to those in your dataset. Names are matched automatically where possible. Press Match Region Names, correct the matches and save. Save (review) at least once, even if nothing needed changing. Clear mapping starts again.

sections.heading: Finish Loading Data
sections.text: On the last step press Finish Loading Data. The app merges the sheets, saves the dataset (see Accepted files for the name and place of the saved copy) and shows Ready for analysis, with a summary (rows loaded, checks passed, fields set, files uploaded, regions mapped). Choose Continue to analysis. Use Edit on the summary to return to any step.

sections.heading: RMNCAH and Vaxx apps
sections.text: DataSuite has two Countdown apps for routine health facility data: the RMNCAH App and the Vaxx App. Both take a country's routine facility data (usually exported with the Data Extractor), check and adjust it, choose denominators, and estimate coverage, inequalities and trends. They follow the same CD2030 analytical framework and share most of their pages, so this guide describes them together. Where the apps differ, the guide shows an RMNCAH and a Vaxx tab; the tab you choose is remembered from page to page.

sections.heading: RMNCAH app
sections.text:
The RMNCAH App within the CD2030 DataSuite is designed to support the analysis of routine health facility data for key RMNCAH indicators.
It provides a standardized framework for transforming raw DHIS2 data into meaningful insights on service coverage, data quality, and equity.

Building on the outputs from the Data Extractor, the RMNCAH App guides users through a structured analytical workflow that includes data validation, adjustment, and indicator computation.
This ensures that analyses are consistent, reproducible, and aligned with the CD2030 methodological approach.

The app enables users to:

- Assess data quality through standardized DQA metrics
- Apply numerator and denominator adjustments
- Generate national and subnational coverage estimates
- Explore inequalities and trends across time and geography
- Produce outputs for reporting, including synthesis reports and visualizations

By integrating methodological rigor with a user-friendly interface, the RMNCAH App facilitates evidence-based decision-making and supports countries in monitoring progress across RMNCAH priorities.

sections.heading: Vaxx app
sections.text:
The Vaxx App is the DataSuite app for immunization coverage and inequalities. It takes a country's routine facility data (usually exported with the Data Extractor), checks and adjusts it, chooses a denominator, and then estimates coverage for routine vaccines, dropout, zero-dose and under-vaccinated children. Coverage can be compared with survey and WUENIC estimates, followed over time, split by region, district, area of residence, maternal education and wealth, and tracked against global targets.

It follows the same CD2030 analytical framework as the RMNCAH App, but is narrowed to immunization: the indicator list, the survey inputs, the adjustment factors and the analysis pages are all immunization-specific.

sections.heading: RMNCAH app users
sections.text: The RMNCAH App is written for the country analytical team of a CD2030 review: monitoring and evaluation officers, HMIS and DHIS2 data managers, programme managers for maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health, and the analysts who prepare annual health sector reviews. You do not need to write code. Everything is done through pages, filters, charts and tables. Analysts who prefer scripting can work on the same saved dataset through the DataSuite chat assistant (see Exports, reports and AI).

sections.heading: Vaxx app users
sections.text:
- Immunization programme managers and national EPI analysts who need routine coverage estimates that are quality-checked and comparable with surveys.
- Analysts in the Countdown immunization coverage and inequalities work, at national and district level.
- Anyone who needs a Word, PDF or PowerPoint report of data quality and coverage for a country.

sections.text:

sections.heading: How it relates to the Data Extractor and the methodology
sections.text:
- The Data Extractor produces the routine data file. The apps start where the extractor stops.
- The methodology chapters explain why each analysis is done and how to interpret it. Every page guide in this section ends with a link to the matching chapter, and the Get Help button in the app opens the same chapters.

sections.heading: Layout and navigation
sections.text:
RMNCAH App navigation panes

- Sidebar. The pages are grouped in sections (see Page groups). Change Language at the top switches the app between English, French and Portuguese.
- Locked pages. Pages are greyed out until they can be used. Load Data is always open. The Denominators and Analysis groups and Output (Reports) unlock only after you have finished loading a dataset and run Data Adjustment.
- Page header. Each page shows its title and a one-line subtitle. Get Help opens the matching methodology (help) chapter. Pages that feed a standard report also show Generate Report. The header also holds the language switch (English, French, Portuguese). Analysis pages show a Denominator row that tells you which denominators the numbers were divided by; it is set on the Denominator Selection page.
- Filter bar. Filters appear as chips at the top of a page, for example Indicator, Admin Level, Performance Threshold or Select Years.
- Chart cards. A card usually has one tab per indicator plus a Custom tab where you pick any other analysis indicator. The card toolbar downloads the chart (Download Plot, PNG) or its numbers (Download Data, Excel), and offers tools to edit labels, change the view or style, and expand the chart.
- Tables. A control marked This table only (year or indicator) changes that table alone. Each table has its own Download Data button.

sections.heading: Recommended order
sections.text:
Countdown analysis workflow

[RMNCAH] The analysis steps page walks through the same sequence and links each step to its methodology chapter.

[Vaxx] - Load the data and finish the wizard.
- Review the five data quality pages, then decide whether to remove years.
- Adjust the data. This unlocks the remaining pages.
- Compare denominators and choose one.
- Read national coverage, inequality, equity and targets, then the sub-national pages.
- Build a report (see Reports).

Methods behind each step are described in the framework chapters: data quality, adjustment, denominators, coverage, equity and sub-national analysis. Indicator definitions are in Indicator definitions.

ai.summary: The RMNCAH and Vaxx apps analyse routine health facility data with the same CD2030 framework: they check data quality, adjust the data, choose denominators, estimate national and sub-national coverage, explore inequalities and produce reports. RMNCAH covers reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health indicators; Vaxx is narrowed to immunization (routine vaccines, dropout, zero-dose and under-vaccinated children). Both start where the Data Extractor stops.

sections.heading: Mortality
sections.text:
This page applies to the RMNCAH app only.

The Mortality group looks at deaths recorded in health facilities: institutional maternal mortality, stillbirths and neonatal deaths before discharge. It has three pages: Institutional Mortality, Mortality Mapping and Mortality Completeness. The method, definitions and formulas are in Mortality.

Mortality figures use the reported numbers of deaths without the reporting-rate and outlier adjustment applied to other indicators (why: Mortality > iMMR and iSBR review). They still depend on the denominator you selected (live births or births). If a value looks like a data entry error, check it in Outlier Detection and treat it with the methodology's guidance (Outlier detection thresholds).

sections.heading: Institutional Mortality
sections.text:
Purpose. Show the level and trend of institutional mortality and check whether it is plausible.

When to use it. First, to see the rates; then use the second card to test data quality.

sections.heading: Open Institutional Mortality
sections.text: It is under Mortality in the Analysis group.

sections.heading: Read the first card, Institutional Mortality
sections.text:
Tabs: Maternal Mortality (per 100,000 live births in facilities), Still Birth Rate and Neonatal Deaths. Dots are regions and the line is the country, by year.

How to read it: Mortality > Institutional mortality levels.

sections.heading: Read the second card, Institutional Mortality DQA
sections.text:
Tabs: Fresh Stillbirths (fresh stillbirths as a percentage of all stillbirths), SBR to Maternal Death Ratio (stillbirths per maternal death) and Neonatal / Maternal Deaths (institutional neonatal deaths per maternal death). Each chart shows the Median and an Expected range, and a note under the chart gives the range.

The ranges and how to read them: Mortality > Expected ranges on the DQA charts and Reading the DQA checks.

Institutional maternal mortality by region and year

Fresh stillbirths as a percentage of total stillbirths

How to interpret. See Mortality > Reading the DQA checks; for neonatal deaths before discharge, Considerations for iSBR.

sections.heading: Mortality Mapping
sections.text:
Purpose. Map institutional mortality across regions.

Filters. Select Years (one or several) and Palette (Greens, Blues, Reds or Purples; the default is Reds).

Tabs: Maternal Mortality and Still Birth Rate. Each map shows the values by region for the selected years, which makes geographic clusters visible.

Institutional maternal mortality by region

How to read the map: Mortality > Geographic distribution.

sections.heading: Mortality Completeness
sections.text:
Purpose. Estimate how completely facilities report deaths, by comparing the reported institutional rate with an expected rate built from UN estimates.

When to use it. After the DQA charts, to judge whether reported mortality can be used at all.

Tabs: Institutional MMR and Institutional SBR. Each chart draws completeness for the lower bound, median and upper bound of the UN estimate, across several assumptions about how much higher community mortality is than institutional mortality. Use Generate Report to open the mortality report.

How it is computed: Mortality > Computing reporting completeness. How to narrow the scenarios with local evidence: Evaluation scenarios and interpretation.

Completeness of facility maternal death reporting

Completeness relies on the UN mortality estimates. Use the built-in country data, or upload your own in the Upload Data step of Getting started.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.text: Pitfalls in interpreting institutional mortality: Mortality > Common pitfalls.

sections.heading: Reports
sections.text:
The Reports page in the Output section builds reports from the loaded dataset. There are two kinds:

Kind | What it is | Files you can download
Document | Pages of text, charts and tables, with an optional cover page and contents | Word (

.docx

) or PDF
Slide deck | Slides with text boxes, charts, tables and pictures | PowerPoint (

.pptx

) or PDF

Charts and tables are drawn from the data every time you preview or download, so a report always reflects the current state of your analysis (years removed, adjustment, denominators). Every report you create is saved in the dataset and listed under Your reports. For downloading single charts and tables, datasets and the AI assistant, see Exports, reports and AI.

Reports are stored inside the dataset file. Creating or editing a report rewrites the saved dataset (the .rds cache), and the report list travels with it. Keep a copy of the dataset before you experiment, and share the dataset if you want a colleague to open your reports.

The page subtitle in the app still says "Word and PDF reports". The code also builds slide decks, and the one-pager is a PowerPoint deck.

sections.heading: Standard reports
sections.text:
A standard report is the Countdown report of one analysis section, rebuilt as editable blocks. It opens as your own copy: change or delete anything. Text blocks written as questions (headed Notes or Interpretations) are prompts for the analyst; replace them with the interpretation agreed at your review meeting.

Each app has its own set of standard reports:

[RMNCAH] Standard report | Kind | What it contains | Page with a

Generate Report

button

Denominator selection | Document | DHIS2 and UN projections of population, live births and under 1, then coverage of Penta3 and institutional live births under each denominator, national and by region | Denominator Selection

National inequality | Document | For institutional live births and Penta3: coverage by region over time, map, equity by wealth and education; then coverage by district | Equity Assessment
Mortality | Document | Institutional maternal (iMMR), stillbirth (iSBR) and neonatal mortality trends, stillbirths per maternal death, completeness of death reporting | Mortality Completeness
Curative health services | Document | Service utilization data quality table, outpatient and inpatient charts and maps, preventive vs curative index | MCH Preventive vs Curative Index

The Vaxx App has no standard reports for mortality, service utilization, health system or private sector, and none for national coverage on its own: those belong to the RMNCAH App (see the RMNCAH tab). National coverage is inside the synthesis chartbook, and you can build a coverage report from blocks (see below).

sections.heading: Finish the prerequisites
sections.text:
Reports stays locked until you have loaded a dataset and run Data Adjustment (see Data preparation).

[RMNCAH] Choose denominators on Denominator Selection first: most charts use them.

[Vaxx] Choose the denominator on Denominator Selection first: the coverage charts use it.

sections.heading: Open it
sections.text: Click Reports under Output, or click Reports in the top header. A Generate Report button in a page header also opens the page and starts the matching standard report.

sections.heading: Choose a report
sections.text: Under Standard reports (documents) or Standard slide decks, click a card. Each card shows how many charts and tables it holds. You can also start from New document or New slide deck (Start blank).

sections.heading: Name it and choose its language
sections.text: A dialog asks for the report name (for example, the report and country), the Report language (English, French or Portuguese) and confirms with Create report. The report language is independent of the app language: the standard text is written in it, and the charts, tables and dates are always drawn in it. You can change it later on the Layout tab; charts and tables are redrawn, but text you wrote yourself is not translated.

sections.heading: Wait for the charts
sections.text: The editor opens at once. Each chart shows Drawing from the dataset and appears one by one. A chart that cannot be drawn shows Could not be drawn with this dataset with the reason.

sections.heading: Set the region, if the report has one
sections.text: For the one-pager (and any chart drawn for one region), pick the region on the Layout tab, under Report, in Region of this report. The first region in alphabetical order is chosen for you. Leave it empty for a national report. To produce a one-pager for every region, duplicate the report from the list and change the region.

sections.heading: Edit, then check
sections.text: Replace the prompts, delete what you do not need, then open Print layout to see the final pages (see below).

sections.heading: Download
sections.text: Choose Download, pick the format and wait for the progress bar (Drawing charts from the dataset, then Writing the Word file, Printing the PDF or Writing the PowerPoint file). The file downloads by itself; Download again is offered if it does not.

sections.heading: The document editor
sections.text:
The Blocks panel (left) differs between the apps:

[RMNCAH] - Blocks panel (left). The Blocks tab lists every chart and table kind grouped by analysis area, with a search box (Search charts, tables, text); Text and layout holds Heading, Sub-heading, Paragraph, Notes box and Page break. Drag a block onto a page, or press + to add it after the selected block. The Outline tab lists the report's structure. A Custom group is announced for charts made for your dataset; it is empty for now.

[Vaxx] - Blocks panel (left). The Blocks tab lists every chart and table kind that exists for the Vaxx indicators, grouped by analysis area (data quality, adjustment, denominators, national, sub-national, region profile), with a search box (Search charts, tables, text). For example Coverage trend: DHIS2 and survey, Districts reaching the target, Coverage map, Equity (from surveys) and Coverage indicators by year (DHIS2), which has a zero-dose and dropout variant for Vaxx datasets. Text and layout holds Heading, Sub-heading, Paragraph, Notes box and Page break. Drag a block onto a page, or press + to add it after the selected block. The Outline tab lists the report's structure.

The rest of the editor is the same in both apps:

- Chart and table settings. Select a block to set what it shows: Indicator, Level (National, Region or District), a variant (in the RMNCAH App, for example Maternal or Child), Year, Region, Width (Full width, Half or Third), a title and Show caption and source. Customize this chart changes text, fonts and colours for this chart in this report only. Charts you customised in the app with Apply to: Report keep that styling.
- Order and removal. Drag a block by its handle, or use Move up, Move down, Duplicate and Delete. Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover edits. Changes save automatically (Saved in the dataset).
- Text. Type directly. Enter starts a paragraph, Shift+Enter a new line. Insert Fields such as {country}, {region}, {first_year}, {latest_year}, {chart_indicator} or coverage values like {penta3_latest}; they are filled in from the data and follow the report language.
- Design. The Design tab holds themes (Countdown, Ministry of Health, Minimal, Formal), colours, fonts, the Cover page (title, subtitle, logos, country flag, editors, date, reference) and Contents. Layout sets page size (A4, Letter, chartbook, poster), orientation, margins, page numbers, header and footer. Browse for Themes builds a theme from a PowerPoint or Word file (.potx, .pptx, .dotx, .docx); downloads are then written from that file.
- Views. Edit, Read mode, Print layout (the exact final pages), Focus and zoom.
- Slide decks use a slide editor with layouts, a slide sorter, speaker notes and text boxes; charts and tables are placed on slides in the same way.

sections.heading: Formats and downloads
sections.text:
Format | Made by | Notes
Word

.docx | The app | Editable. On Windows with Word installed, Word also fills in the contents page and embeds fonts
PDF of a document | Made from the Word file by Microsoft Word or LibreOffice, so pages match Word exactly | If neither is installed, Chrome, Edge or Chromium prints it: close to the Word file, but pages can differ
PowerPoint

.pptx | The app | Text, charts and tables stay editable in PowerPoint
PDF of a slide deck | PowerPoint or LibreOffice | Not possible without one of them

The file is named after the country, the report name and the date, for example Kenya_Synthesis_chartbook_2026-09-26.docx, and is saved wherever your browser or DataSuite saves downloads. A document cannot be exported as PowerPoint, nor a deck as Word.

sections.heading: Prerequisites that change report content
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] - Removed years and adjustment decide the numbers in every coverage, adjustment and mortality chart.
- Denominators chosen on Denominator Selection are used by the coverage charts. Without them, the coverage-by-denominator trend chart says Choose the denominators first.
- Surveys. Equity charts and facility-versus-survey comparisons need the survey files you loaded.
- Country reference data. The FPET chart needs family planning estimates for the country.

[Vaxx] - Removed years and adjustment decide the numbers in every coverage and adjustment chart.
- The denominator chosen on Denominator Selection is used by the coverage charts. Without it, the coverage-by-denominator trend chart says Choose the denominators first.
- Surveys. Equity charts and facility-versus-survey comparisons need the survey files you loaded in the wizard.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
Symptom | Likely cause and fix
Could not be drawn with this dataset

in a block | The dataset lacks the data. Read the reason after it, load the missing file or delete the block. The same text appears in the exported file
Choose a region | A regional chart has no region: set

Region of this report
No district coverage for ... in ... | Pick a year and region that have data
Final pages or PDF fail, or say a converter is missing | Install Microsoft Word or LibreOffice on the computer running the app. Word download still works
Slide deck PDF fails | Needs PowerPoint or LibreOffice. Download PowerPoint instead

sections.heading: Tips for stakeholders
sections.text: What to settle, state and fill in before a report goes to stakeholders: Dissemination > Preparing reports for stakeholders. In the app, the cover is on the Design tab, the language is the Report language (also on the Layout tab), Print layout shows the final pages, and duplicating a report from the list gives a one-pager for another region.

sections.heading: What this page does not cover
sections.text: Page notes added with the Notes button are not part of the report builder as far as the source shows. The Custom chart group of the RMNCAH App is a placeholder. Where DataSuite saves downloaded files depends on your browser or desktop settings, which the report code does not control.

ai.summary: The Reports page of the RMNCAH and Vaxx apps builds documents (Word or PDF) and slide decks (PowerPoint or PDF) from the loaded dataset, from the app's standard reports or a blank page. Charts and tables are redrawn from the data each time, and every report is saved in the dataset: creating or editing a report rewrites the saved .rds, so keep a copy before experimenting. The Vaxx app has fewer standard reports than the RMNCAH app.

Vaxx: no standard reports for mortality, service utilization, health system, private sector or national coverage on its own; those are RMNCAH reports (#standard-reports)

PDF of a document needs Word or LibreOffice (else a browser prints it); PDF of a deck needs PowerPoint or LibreOffice; a document cannot be exported as PowerPoint, nor a deck as Word (#formats-and-downloads)
Removed years, adjustment, denominators and survey files change report content; RMNCAH: also country reference data for FPET (#prerequisites-that-change-report-content)
Dissemination is covered in Dissemination (/en/docs/methodology/dissemination/), including which reports stakeholders ask for and how to prepare them
notCovered: Page notes from the Notes button; the Custom chart group (RMNCAH) is a placeholder; where downloads are saved (#what-this-page-does-not-cover)

sections.heading: Service utilization and health system
sections.text:
This page applies to the RMNCAH app only.

Two groups in the Analysis section look beyond coverage of RMNCAH interventions. Service Utilization studies how much outpatient and inpatient care children receive. Health System Performance relates services to the inputs of the health system: facilities, beds, workforce and the private sector. Both need Data Adjustment to have been run. Methods: Service utilization and Health system performance.

sections.heading: Service Utilization
sections.text: Suggested order: check the data first, then read national and sub-national use, then the combined index.

sections.heading: Service Utilization DQA
sections.text:
Purpose. Judge whether OPD and IPD data are good enough to interpret.

Filter. A region selector (Select All for national results).

The page shows one table, Data Quality Metrics, by year. Its rows are the percent of expected monthly facility reports, the districts meeting the reporting threshold you set on Reporting Rate, the percent of non-missing OPD and IPD monthly values, the districts with no missing OPD or IPD values, OPD values that are not extreme outliers, districts with no OPD extreme outliers, the ratio of OPD to IPD for children under 5, and the percent of OPD and IPD that concerns children under 5. Download Plot and Download Data are in the toolbar.

Read this table before the utilization trends: Service utilization > Common pitfalls.

Service utilization DQA

sections.heading: National Utilization
sections.text:
Tabs: OPD Visits (visits per person per year, all ages and under 5), IPD Admissions, Under 5 (share of OPD visits and IPD admissions that are children under 5), Case Fatality Rate (under 5 and all ages) and Deaths (proportion of deaths that are under 5). A second card, with Select Years and a Palette (default Purples), maps OPD Map and IPD Map by region.

How to read it: Service utilization > Outpatient service utilization, Case fatality rate and Interpretation.

OPD visits

sections.heading: Sub-National Utilization
sections.text:
Choose a region (or Select All) to see the same tabs for that area, plus a second card, Sub-National Utilization, with the tabs OPD Visits and IPD Admissions showing the distribution across Admin 1 regions: OPD per child under 5 per year and IPD admissions per 100 children under 5.

Sub-national distribution of OPD

sections.heading: MCH Preventive vs Curative Index
sections.text:
Each dot is an Admin 1 region. The horizontal axis is the MCH Preventive services index and the vertical axis the Curative service use index. Median lines divide the plot into four quadrants: low or high preventive, and low or high curative. Generate Report opens the service utilization report.

What the indices measure: Service utilization > MCH preventive vs curative index. How to read the quadrants: Reading the MCH preventive vs curative index.

MCH preventive versus curative index

sections.heading: National Health System
sections.text:
A table of health system indicators for the latest year, with the columns Indicator, Value and Unit, in three sections: Health infrastructure (facility density per 10,000, share of facilities that are hospitals, hospital density per 100,000, inpatient bed density per 10,000), Health workforce (workforce density per 10,000 and the ratio of nurse-midwives per physician) and Role of private sector (share of private and of NGO facilities). Download the table or its image from the toolbar. Indicator definitions: Health system performance > Input indicators and analytical benchmarks.

National health system

sections.heading: Sub-National Health System
sections.text:
Tabs: Health Facility Density, Hospital Density, Workforce Density and Bed Density. Bars show each region against the National average line. For facilities, beds and workforce a dashed Target benchmark is drawn and bars are coloured Meets benchmark or Below benchmark; hospital density has no benchmark line.

The benchmark values: Health system performance > Benchmarks drawn in the apps.

Health facility density by region

sections.heading: PHC Performance
sections.text:
Tabs: Health Facility Density and Workforce Density. Each scatter plot relates an input to a service index for the Admin 1 regions. Dashed median lines split the chart into quadrants, for example high density with a low service index. Unusual regions are labelled.

How to read it: Health system performance > Interpretation and Common pitfalls.

Health system by region

sections.heading: Public/Private Share
sections.text:
The top card shows the ownership of health facilities as percentages of Private, NGO and Public. Below it, tabs National and Urban/Rural show the public and private split nationally and by area of residence.

The chart title currently reads Ownership of health facilities, 2024 (DHIS2). Check that the year matches your data before quoting it.

Public and private share

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.text: Pitfalls in interpreting these results: Service utilization > Common pitfalls and Health system performance > Common pitfalls.

ai.summary: Service Utilization studies outpatient and inpatient care for children; Health System Performance relates services to facilities, beds, workforce and the private sector. Both need Data Adjustment. Check the Service Utilization DQA before reading utilization trends.
rules: Methods, thresholds and how to read the results are in Service utilization (/en/docs/methodology/service-utilisation/)
Health system methods, benchmarks and pitfalls are in Health system performance (/en/docs/methodology/health-system/)
interpretation: Service Utilization DQA: one Data Quality Metrics table by year for OPD and IPD, to check before reading utilization trends (#service-utilization-dqa)
National Utilization: tabs OPD Visits, IPD Admissions, Under 5, Case Fatality Rate and Deaths, with OPD and IPD maps (#national-utilization)
MCH Preventive vs Curative Index: each Admin 1 region placed by the two indices, in four quadrants split by median lines (#mch-preventive-vs-curative-index)
Sub-National Health System: region bars against the national average, with a Target benchmark and Meets or Below benchmark (#sub-national-health-system)
PHC Performance: an input against a service index by Admin 1 region, in quadrants split by median lines (#phc-performance)

sections.heading: Sub-national analysis
sections.text:
The Sub-National Analysis group repeats the national analysis for regions (Admin 1) and districts (Admin 2) (why: Subnational analysis > Subnational coverage). It has three pages: Sub-National Coverage, Sub-National Inequality and Coverage Target. The method is described in Subnational analysis.

These pages need adjusted data and use the same denominators as the national pages (see Denominators); in the Vaxx app, this is the vaccination denominator chosen there. In the Vaxx app, their indicator tabs and the Custom Check tab work as described in Coverage, equity and targets.

Expect more noise at district level than at region level: see Subnational analysis > Coverage estimates at Admin1 and Admin2.

sections.heading: Sub-National Coverage
sections.text:
Purpose. Compare DHIS2 and survey coverage estimates for each region or district.

When to use it. After National Coverage, to find the areas behind the national figure.

sections.heading: Open Sub-National Coverage
sections.text: It is in the Sub-National Analysis group.

sections.heading: Set the geography
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] Choose the Admin Level. With Admin 1 a region selector appears, and with Admin 2 a district selector, so that you can focus on one area.

[Vaxx] Use Admin Level (Admin 1 or Admin 2) and the region selector. Choose Admin 1 with no region to see regions, or pick a region to see its districts. At Admin 2 the selector can also pick a district.

sections.heading: Pick an indicator
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] Pick an indicator tab: ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births, Low Birth Weight, Pentavalent 3, Measles 1, FP Projection or Custom for any other indicator.

[Vaxx] Choose a tab, or Custom Check for any Vaxx indicator, including dropout, zero-dose and under-vaccinated.

sections.heading: Read the chart
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] The title names the area, for example the coverage estimates of the selected region. Lines show the DHIS2 estimate and the survey estimate, and the caption names the denominator used. Download Plot and Download Data are in the toolbar.

[Vaxx] The chart is titled "... Coverage Estimates" for the selected area and shows the DHIS2 estimate, with the WUENIC and survey estimates where they exist for that geography. The caption gives the denominator.

[RMNCAH] Sub-national coverage

How to interpret. See Subnational analysis > Subnational coverage. The region's Reporting Rate is on the data quality pages; check it before drawing conclusions.

[Vaxx] Sub-national coverage

Survey and WUENIC estimates appear only where they exist for the selected geography, so some charts show DHIS2 alone.

sections.heading: Sub-National Inequality
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] Purpose. Show how far each region (or each district inside a region) is from the national or regional figure, year by year.

Filters. Admin Level and, at Admin 1, a region selector to zoom in on one region.

Tabs are ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births, Low Birth Weight, Pentavalent 3, Measles 1 and Custom. Each dot is a sub-national unit (Coverage at subnational unit) and the line is the national or, when a region is chosen, the regional coverage. How to read the spread, and the MADM that summarises it: Subnational analysis > Inequality.

Sub-national inequality

[Vaxx] Shows how coverage differs between units inside one geography.

- Filters: Admin Level and region. Each chart plots the coverage of every sub-national unit by year (legend "Coverage at subnational unit") against the coverage of the selected region or the country (legend "National Coverage", or the region name followed by "Coverage").
- The subtitle says which units are shown: "Subnational unit: admin 1 level", "district level" or the region name.
- Tabs and the Custom Check tab work as on the national page.

Use it to find districts that sit far below their region, and to see whether the gap narrows over time. How to read it: Subnational analysis > Inequality.

sections.heading: Coverage Target
sections.text:
[RMNCAH] Purpose. Show the percentage of districts in a region that meet a coverage target, by year.

Filter. A region selector. The level is fixed to districts.

Tabs are ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births and Vaccine. The targets are the same as on the national page (Subnational analysis > Target values). A table under the chart lists the districts that reach the target for the indicator chosen in its This table only control.

How to read the percentages: Subnational analysis > Progress towards targets.

Sub-national coverage against targets

[Vaxx] The share of districts in a region meeting the global targets.

- Choose the region (this page has no admin level filter: the unit is always the district).
- Read the two tabs. Vaccine covers BCG, Pentavalent 3 and Measles 1. Dropout covers Penta 1 to Penta 3 and Penta 3 to Measles 1. The thresholds are in Subnational analysis > Target values.
- The chart title, "Percentage of districts in (region name) meeting the ... target", shows the threshold used. Bars are percentages by year and indicator.
- The table lists the districts meeting the target for the indicator and year you select. Download it as Excel with the table's download button.

sections.heading: Interpretation and pitfalls
sections.text:
How to read these results and the pitfalls to avoid: Subnational analysis > Interpretation and Common pitfalls. To cross-check a district that looks implausible, use Data quality; to test another denominator, go back to Denominators.

- In the Vaxx app, changing the admin level resets the region selection.

[RMNCAH] Next: Advanced analysis.

[Vaxx] Next: Exports, reports and AI.

ai.summary: Three Sub-National Analysis pages, Sub-National Coverage, Sub-National Inequality and Coverage Target, repeat the national analysis for regions (Admin 1) and districts (Admin 2), where programme action is usually targeted. They use the same adjusted data and denominators as the national pages (in Vaxx, the chosen vaccination denominator). Expect more noise at district level than at region level.
options: Coverage Target tabs: ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births and Vaccine (RMNCAH); Vaccine (BCG, Pentavalent 3, Measles 1) and Dropout (Penta 1 to Penta 3, Penta 3 to Measles 1) (Vaxx); region selector, level fixed to districts (#coverage-target)
rules: RMNCAH: the region's Reporting Rate is on the Data quality page; check it before drawing conclusions (#sub-national-coverage)
Cross-check a district that looks implausible in Data quality (#interpretation-and-pitfalls)
Vaxx: changing the admin level resets the region selection (#interpretation-and-pitfalls)
The target thresholds are in Subnational analysis (/en/docs/methodology/subnational#target-values)
How to read these pages, and the pitfalls, are in Subnational analysis (/en/docs/methodology/subnational#interpretation)
interpretation: Sub-National Coverage: DHIS2 and survey lines for the chosen area (in Vaxx also WUENIC, only where they exist for that geography); the caption names the denominator (#read-the-chart)
Sub-National Inequality: dots are sub-national units, the line is national or regional coverage (#sub-national-inequality)
Coverage Target: percentage of districts in a region meeting the target, by year; the table lists the districts meeting it (#coverage-target)

sections.heading: Downloading data
sections.text:
Once login, metadata retrieval, and mapping are complete, the extractor can begin data download.
Instead of relying on a single large DHIS2 request, the extractor is designed to handle extraction in smaller and more manageable batches.
This approach lowers the risk of timeouts for large download requests, thus reducing the chances of incomplete downloads.

Large extractions still need planning:

- Even with caching and chunked processing, very large downloads may take time depending on server performance, user permissions, internet stability, and the size of the requested organization unit and period ranges.

sections.heading: Go to the Downloads Manager and click + New Download Task
sections.text: Downloads Manager with the New Download Task button

sections.heading: Configure the download parameters
sections.text:
Select the mapping (Mapping Configuration, in case you have multiple mappings), the period (Date Range, start and end dates), the Frequency (monthly or yearly; shown for Custom mappings only), the Admin Level and, optionally, a Sub-region to limit the download to one area, then click Start Download.

Configure Download Task dialog

Countdown download configuration:

- Date Range: use the last five years (for example, January 1st 2020 to December 31st 2025).
- Admin Level: use Level 3.

sections.heading: Export the data
sections.text:
When the task is complete, it moves to Recent History. In its Actions column, click Export to Excel to save the workbook that the RMNCAH and Vaxx apps load (sheets Service_data, Population_data, Reporting_completeness and Admin_data), or Export to JSON. A failed task can be restarted with Retry Download. On a DHIS2 server that uses the Ethiopian calendar, Excel labels chooses Ethiopic or Gregorian period labels for the Excel file.

Caching is not only useful for metadata. It also helps the extractor preserve progress and reduce unnecessary repeated work where extraction tasks are interrupted or revisited.

This improves reliability in practical field conditions, especially when:

- internet connectivity is unstable,
- DHIS2 response times vary,
- analysts need to rerun the same extract after refining mappings,
- teams want a reproducible process with less manual repetition.

Tip: If you are testing mappings, validate the metadata and structure first using a smaller extraction range before launching a full national, multi-year download.

sections.heading: Open the CD2030 DHIS2 Data Extractor
sections.text:
Open it from the Welcome page with Open Data Extractor (see Getting started).

The first step is to connect the application to the relevant DHIS2 server. Users provide the DHIS2 instance URL together with their username and password.
Once authenticated, the extractor can read only the metadata and data that the logged-in user is already authorized to access in that DHIS2 environment.

DHIS2 login screen of the Data Extractor

Important: Access rights are controlled by DHIS2, not by the extractor. If a user cannot see a dataset, organization unit, or indicator in DHIS2, the extractor will not bypass those permissions.

sections.heading: Enter valid login credentials
sections.text:
- Start by typing your country's name. From the second letter, known DHIS2 servers whose URL, name or country match appear, and you can select yours. If your country's DHIS2 instance URL is not shown, type it in full.
- Then enter your DHIS2 Username and password and click Login.

Server URL suggestions on the login screen

Tip: Start by confirming the DHIS2 base URL before entering credentials. A correct URL prevents login failures caused by pointing to the wrong server environment.

sections.heading: Cache metadata
sections.text:
Done automatically following a successful login, this loads and locally caches the metadata needed for mapping and extraction.
After login, the extractor retrieves the metadata needed to understand the structure of the DHIS2 instance.
This can include items such as organization units, data elements, indicators, category option combinations, datasets, and other configuration objects required for mapping and extraction.

Data Extractor dashboard after login

If you think the DHIS2 data might have changed since the last session, click Sync Meta to ensure the metadata is updated.

Why caching helps:

- Metadata caching reduces repeated calls to DHIS2, speeds up setup for later runs, and creates a smaller download footprint because the extractor only needs to refresh what is necessary.
- Rather than downloading the same metadata repeatedly for every step, the extractor caches it locally for reuse during the session and in later work where appropriate.

sections.heading: CD2030 DHIS2 Data Extractor
sections.text:
The CD2030 DHIS2 Data Extractor helps teams connect to DHIS2, prepare metadata, map indicators, and download routine data in a way that is more stable and easier to reproduce than manual extraction.

It is designed to support large, multi-period downloads while reducing server strain, avoiding unnecessary repeat requests, and preserving progress through local caching.

Access disclaimer: The CD2030 DHIS2 Data Extractor does not allow unauthorized access to DHIS2 data.

sections.heading: What the extractor does
sections.text:
The extractor supports a practical end-to-end workflow:

This process helps analysts produce a cleaner and more reproducible starting point for downstream analysis in DataSuite.

The Excel workbook it exports is the routine data file that the RMNCAH and Vaxx apps load; for what that data must contain, see Analysis setup in the methodology and the Indicator definitions.

sections.heading: Log in to DHIS2
sections.text: Connect to the correct DHIS2 instance using your server URL and valid account credentials.

sections.heading: Cache metadata
sections.text: Temporarily cache (store) metadata locally for fast access and efficient downloading.

sections.heading: Choose a mapping mode
sections.text: Use Countdown mapping for the harmonized MNCH template or Custom mapping for other programs.

sections.heading: Download data
sections.text: Run extraction with smaller requests and reuse cached metadata to minimize repeat downloads.

sections.heading: Mapping configuration
sections.text:
Mapping defines what data to extract from DHIS2 and how it is structured for analysis.
It is the core step in the Data Extractor workflow in that it fetches indicators of interest,
maps them to the corresponding DHIS2 data sources, and standardizes outputs for DataSuite apps and other analyses.

sections.heading: Navigating the CD2030 DHIS2 Data Extractor
sections.text: Once successfully logged in, the following views help in navigating the CD2030 DHIS2 Data Extractor.

sections.heading: Dashboard
sections.text: Data Extractor dashboard

sections.heading: Mappings Manager
sections.text:
Mappings Manager listing saved mappings

The Mappings Manager is the central place to:

- View all saved mappings
- Search mappings by name or ID
- Create a new mapping

sections.heading: Key actions
sections.text:
- New Mapping: start a new configuration
- Search bar: locate existing mappings
- Actions column: edit, export as JSON, clone, or delete the selected mapping

sections.heading: Downloads Manager
sections.text:
Downloads Manager showing a download in progress

The Downloads Manager is where you create download tasks and follow their progress (see downloading data).

sections.heading: Click New Mapping
sections.text: New mapping screen in draft mode

sections.heading: Configure the mapping
sections.text:
Define the mapping name, description, and mapping mode.

Important: Use a clear naming convention. For example:

- Mapping name: CAM2026_CountryName
- Description: MNH Indicators for CAM 2026 Workshop

sections.heading: Select the mapping mode
sections.text: Choose Countdown or Custom in the Mapping Mode field. Both modes are described below.

sections.heading: Mapping modes
sections.text:
Mapping is the stage where DHIS2 source metadata is linked to the structure needed for downstream analysis.
The extractor supports two mapping approaches depending on the use case.

sections.heading: Countdown option
sections.text:
The Countdown option maps indicators and related metadata to the Countdown harmonized MNCH data template.
This is the preferred approach when teams are preparing data for Countdown to 2030 workflows and want a standardized structure that aligns with the embedded resource template used by the application.

This option is useful when:

- the analysis is focused on harmonized MNCH indicators,
- teams want consistency across countries or time periods,
- outputs are intended for Countdown-aligned analytical workflows.

Recommended for standardization: Use the Countdown option when your goal is to produce data aligned with the harmonized MNCH template embedded in the extractor resources.

sections.heading: Custom option
sections.text:
The Custom option allows users to create mappings for other programs or use cases that do not fit the Countdown harmonized template. This gives teams flexibility to work with country-specific program structures, additional service areas, or bespoke indicator sets.

This option is useful when:

- the program area goes beyond the Countdown MNCH scope,
- users need a country-defined mapping structure,
- the extraction supports another analytical workflow outside the standard harmonized template.

Flexible mapping: Choose the Custom option when you need to prepare data for other health programs, local reporting needs, or non-Countdown analytical pipelines.

Mapping summary

There are currently two mapping modes:

- Countdown: this mode has a predefined list of MNCH indicators and structure, as in the harmonized data template.
- Custom: fully user-defined configuration, where the user can download any data that they have access rights to.

Changing the mapping mode clears all the indicators and their configuration from the mapping you are editing, whether or not it was saved; the app asks you to confirm first (Yes, Clear Indicators). Choose the mapping mode before you add indicators.

sections.heading: Indicators configuration
sections.text:
The Indicators Configuration panel is where the indicators of a mapping are defined. Each indicator block has an Internal Name and a Target Export Code, and is linked to the DHIS2 data elements, indicators, or datasets that feed it (Source Configuration). Click Save Mapping to store your changes.

In Countdown mode, the indicators follow the harmonized MNCH template and are marked COUNTDOWN. Search and add the DHIS2 sources for each indicator.

Indicators Configuration in Countdown mode

In Custom mode, you define the indicators yourself, add the DHIS2 sources, and choose which category option combinations (disaggregations) to include.

Indicators Configuration in Custom mode with a data element source and its disaggregation

sections.heading: DataSuite applications
sections.text:
The CD2030 DataSuite includes a set of integrated applications designed to support the analysis of routine health facility data.
Each app plays a specific role within the analytical workflow, from data extraction to analysis and reporting.

App | Use it to | Input
Data Extractor | Pull routine data out of DHIS2 and map it to standard indicators | A DHIS2 instance
RMNCAH App | Analyse reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health indicators end to end | .xls

,

.xlsx

,

.dta

,

.rds
Vaxx App | Analyse immunization coverage and inequalities | .xls

,

.xlsx

,

.dta

,

.rds
Pooled App | Pool the saved analyses of several countries or datasets for regional comparison | A folder of

.rds

sections.heading: CD2030 Data Extractor
sections.text:
The Data Extractor connects to DHIS2 systems and allows users to extract and map routine health facility data into standardized formats for analysis.

Go to Data Extractor →

sections.heading: RMNCAH App
sections.text:
The RMNCAH App supports analysis across reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health indicators, applying the standardized CD2030 analytical approach. It covers data quality, denominators, coverage, equity and sub-national analysis, and adds Bayesian analysis, continuum of care, family planning, mortality, service utilization and health system pages.

Go to RMNCAH App →

sections.heading: Vaxx App
sections.text:
The Vaxx App focuses on immunization. It follows the same analytical stages as the RMNCAH App (data quality, adjustment, denominators, coverage, inequality and targets, national and sub-national) for immunization indicators.

Go to Vaxx App →

sections.heading: Pooled App
sections.text:
The Pooled App is used for regional and multi-country analysis. It loads the caches saved by the RMNCAH and Vaxx apps from a folder, lets you choose the domain (RMNCAH or Immunization), processes the selected dataset and exports the pooled result as CSV or Excel.

Go to Pooled App →

sections.heading: Exporting results
sections.text: Pooled can export a single table as CSV or Excel, or a selected piece of the pooled file in several formats. Values that are missing are written as empty cells.

sections.heading: Quick downloads of one table
sections.text:
- On a dataset page, use Download and choose CSV file or Excel file. The export is the table for the tab you are viewing, with the Countries and Years filters applied.
- On All datasets, the CSV and Excel buttons export the table currently selected in the list, also filtered.

Format | File name | Contents
CSV | the table name and date, for example

Coverage_-_National_2026-01-31.csv | One table, header row, one row per country, year and area
Excel | pooled_rmncah_2026-01-31.xlsx | One sheet named after the table

sections.heading: Extract a piece
sections.text:
Use Extract a piece when you need several tables, or only part of them. The chips at the top choose Datasets, Countries and Years; choosing nothing means all. Under Columns, keep All columns or choose the columns per dataset: country, year and area columns are always kept. The Preview shows up to six rows per dataset.

The Get the piece card counts datasets, countries, years and rows, then offers three formats:

Format | Result
CSV | One CSV for one dataset, or a

.zip

with one CSV per dataset for several
Excel | One workbook with one sheet per dataset
Pooled file | A smaller

.rds

you can reopen in Pooled

Files are named with the domain and date, for example pooled_rmncah_2026-01-31_piece.zip or _piece.xlsx. Sheet names are limited to 31 characters and the characters not allowed in Excel sheet names are replaced by spaces. Excel sheets have a bold header row, a frozen first row and automatic column widths. Explore this piece opens the result in the app. Start again resets all filters and columns.

Excel and CSV files do not contain the build log. To keep the list of countries, the files that were left out and the log, keep the pooled .rds from Build pooled file.

sections.heading: What is inside the pooled file
sections.text: The .rds is a plain R list, not a country cache. It holds domain, the creation time, the app version, a table of countries (country, ISO3, source file, warning), a table of left_out files with reasons, datasets (one table per dataset) and a time-stamped log. Tables are ordered as in the app's dataset list: Parameters and score, Indicator coverage, Coverage, Mortality, Service utilization, Data quality, Denominators, Estimates and surveys, Equity, Health systems.

sections.heading: Next steps for analysis
sections.text:
- Read the CSV or Excel file in R, Stata, Python or Excel. country and iso3 identify the country, and coverage columns already share names across countries.
- For a full analysis in R, read the pooled file with readRDS() and work on pooled$datasets.
- Compare your results with the methods in the analytical framework, including national coverage.
- For issues with a single country, return to its cache in the RMNCAH App, fix it, save, and rebuild the pooled file.

sections.heading: Using the DataSuite chat assistant
sections.text: The DataSuite chat assistant works on a single country's dataset open in the RMNCAH or Vaxx app; see the AI assistant page. The pooled file has a different structure (a list of tables): ask the assistant to read the file and analyse its datasets directly, and check the results against the tables you downloaded.

Compare results with the methods of the framework, including National coverage (/en/docs/methodology/coverage/)

The chat assistant works on one country's dataset open in RMNCAH or Vaxx; for the pooled file, ask it to read the file and analyse its datasets directly, and check against downloaded tables (#using-the-datasuite-chat-assistant)

sections.heading: Pooled App overview
sections.text:
The Pooled App combines the saved datasets of several countries into one file, then lets you explore, compare and export the pooled tables. It is the DataSuite tool for regional and multi-country analysis: instead of opening each country one at a time, you load their saved caches together and work on all of them side by side.

Pooled does not replace the country apps. The RMNCAH App and the Vaxx App are where a country's data is uploaded, checked, adjusted and analysed. Pooled starts from what those apps have already saved.

sections.heading: When to use Pooled
sections.text:
You want to... | Use
Check, adjust and analyse one country's facility data | RMNCAH or Vaxx App
Put several countries side by side (coverage, sources, trends) | Pooled App
Get one table containing all countries for a regional report | Pooled App
Extract only some countries, years or columns for another tool | Pooled App

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.text:
- A set of .rds files, one per country, saved by the RMNCAH or Vaxx App. See Preparing caches.
- All files should belong to the same data domain: RMNCAH or Immunization (VAXX). You choose the domain once, before loading.
- Enough memory: the app accepts up to 2 GB of selected files at a time, and reads them one after another.

Pooled keeps only the analysis tables (coverage, data quality, denominators, surveys and so on). The raw facility-by-month data is left out, which keeps the pooled file small.

sections.heading: How the app is organised
sections.text:
The sidebar has one section, Pooling, with two parts.

Build pooled file is a four-step wizard:

- Choose datasets: the domain, what to include, and the files.
- Loading files: each file is read and reported as loaded, loaded with a warning, or failed.
- Review results: decide what to do about warnings and failures.
- File created: download the pooled .rds or go straight to exploring it.

Explore pooled data opens a pooled file and offers these pages:

Page | What it shows
Open a file | Use the file you just built, or upload one made earlier
Parameters | The settings and survey values each country brings
Overall score | The data quality score of each country
Indicator coverage | Coverage by indicator: national, Admin 1, District
Coverage | Coverage with each country's chosen denominators
Mortality | Facility maternal and newborn deaths (RMNCAH domain)
Service utilization | Outpatient and inpatient use, children under 5 (RMNCAH domain)
Compare countries | Continuum of care, source triangulation, level and change, trends
All datasets | Every table in the file, including those without their own page
Extract a piece | Pull chosen datasets, countries, years and columns into a new file

sections.heading: Preparing caches
sections.text: Pooled reads the caches that the country apps save. A cache is an .rds file that holds a country's dataset together with everything computed on it: adjusted data, coverage, data quality results and the choices made in the analysis. Good pooled results depend on well-prepared caches, so it is worth a few minutes to get them right.

sections.heading: Producing a cache
sections.text:
- Open the RMNCAH App (or the Vaxx App) and upload the country's data. The data usually comes from the Data Extractor.
- Work through the analysis: data quality checks, data preparation and adjustment, and denominator selection. See the analytical framework.
- The app saves the cache as an .rds file. When the country's data was uploaded from a spreadsheet or Stata file, the cache is written next to the source file with the same name and an .rds extension. If that .rds already exists, it is loaded again instead of a new one being created.

Repeat for each country, using the same app and the same domain for all of them.

Complete the adjustment and denominator steps before pooling. A cache that is not adjusted still loads, but Pooled warns that its tables use unadjusted data, and coverage will not be comparable with countries that were adjusted.

sections.heading: What makes a cache loadable
sections.text:
For each file, Pooled opens it as a Countdown cache for the domain you chose and then checks:

- The file can be read by R. A damaged file, or one saved by a newer version of R, is reported as unreadable.
- The cache contains a country name. Files without a country or without adjusted data are reported as "Not a Countdown dataset".
- At least one table can be built. Standard tables that cannot be built produce a warning that lists them.

The country and its ISO3 code come from inside the cache, not from the file name.

sections.heading: Naming and folders
sections.text:
- Only files ending in .rds (any letter case) are used. Other files are listed as skipped.
- Put all the countries you want to pool in one folder. Selecting a folder adds every .rds file inside it.
- Keep a clear name, ideally with the date at the end, for example Kenya_master_adj_dataset_20250918.rds. Pooled reads the last run of eight digits in the name as the file date (year, month, day). If there is none, the file's modified time is used.
- Keep one file per country. If two selected files are for the same country (matched by ISO3 code), Pooled keeps the one with the newer date and leaves the other out, with a reason in the log.
- Remove old versions and unrelated .rds files from the folder, or untick them in step 1.

sections.heading: Compatibility notes
sections.text:
- All caches must be loadable by the version of cd2030.core installed with DataSuite (the Pooled package requires version 1.1.0 or later). Caches carry an internal data version, so if an old file fails to load, open and re-save it in the country app first.
- Countries can have different tables. Data quality or survey tables, for example, may exist for some countries only. Pooled records what each file lacks and flags it in the review step rather than failing.
- If the columns of one table differ between countries in type, they are combined as text and a note is written to the file log.

Next: Using the app.

sections.heading: Using the app
sections.text: This page walks through building a pooled file and exploring it. Make sure your caches are ready first: Preparing caches.

sections.heading: Launch Pooled
sections.text: Start Pooled from the DataSuite apps. When DataSuite starts it with a folder selected, every .rds file in that folder is already added to the file list and a banner shows how many files were pre-loaded. The app opens on Build pooled file. Most Pooled pages and buttons are currently shown in English whatever the language selected.

sections.heading: Choose the datasets (step 1 of 4)
sections.text:
Choose the countries' saved datasets

- Data domain: RMNCAH or Immunization (VAXX). This decides which tables the pooled file contains. With Immunization, the tables that only exist for RMNCAH (mortality and service utilization) are not built.
- What to include: Everything in each dataset adds WUENIC, surveys, denominators, data quality and more. Standard tables only keeps just the tables that Explore has pages for.
- Select files to pick several .rds files at once, or Select a folder to add every .rds file in it. A file with the same name replaces the earlier one in the list.

Each listed file has a tick to include it and a button to remove it. The counter shows the total size against the 2 GB limit. Clear all empties the list. Click Load N files.

sections.heading: Load the files (step 2 of 4)
sections.text:
Loading the selected files

Files are read one at a time and each shows its result as it finishes, with an overall progress bar and four counters: Loaded, Loaded with a warning, Failed, Still to load. You can leave the page open while it runs. Cancel loading returns to step 1; a failed file has a retry option. Then click Review results.

sections.heading: Review and confirm (step 3 of 4)
sections.text:
Review results before combining

The Needs your attention list explains every warning and failure. Typical messages:

Message | Meaning and fix
Not adjusted yet, so its tables use unadjusted data | Finish the adjustment in the country app, save, and reload
N of M standard tables could not be built | The cache lacks some analysis; open it in the country app
Has N of the M tables the loaded files have | Other countries have extra tables this one lacks; usually fine
Another file for the country is newer | Duplicate country; the newer file is used
Not a Countdown dataset | The file has no country or adjusted data; it is not a country cache
Could not read the file | Damaged, or saved by a newer R; re-save it

You can leave a file out. Click Combine N files. If some files are left out, a dialog confirms and notes that they are recorded in the file's log with the reason.

sections.heading: File created (step 4 of 4)
sections.text:
File created, ready to explore or download

The app reports the number of countries and datasets and lists each table with its row count. The file is named pooled_rmncah_ (or pooled_vaccine_) followed by the date, ending in .rds. Use Download .rds to keep it, or Explore this file. Build another file starts again.

The pooled file is built in temporary storage for the session. Download the .rds if you want to open it again later.

sections.heading: Explore pooled data
sections.text:
Open a file on Open a file: use the one just built, or upload a pooled .rds made earlier. Only files made by Build pooled file are accepted; any other .rds is rejected with "This is not a pooled file". After opening, the app jumps to the first page that has data.

Every dataset page has the same layout: a file bar (name, countries, datasets, Change file, Download), Countries and Years filters, tabs for National, Admin 1 and District where the table has them, a summary strip (Rows, Countries, Years, Columns), graphs, and a searchable Data table. The Countries and Years filters are shared by all pages, and choosing none means all.

Pages with numbers also have a Measure filter. Graphs use one line or bar per country, with a fixed colour per country. For Admin 1 and District tables the graphs show the median across areas.

- Parameters: settings and survey values per country, with survey coverage dots, neonatal mortality and survey year.

Parameters page

- Overall score: ranking, and a heatmap of the parts of the score.

Overall score page

- Indicator coverage and Coverage: trend over time, ranking of the latest year, and either spread across districts or a change-since-first-year table.

Coverage page

- Mortality and Service utilization: trend, ranking and change.
- Compare countries: four tabs. Continuum of care is a heatmap of the latest facility coverage from the first antenatal visit to the vaccines. Source triangulation shows facility, survey and WUENIC values for DTP3 and MCV1 with the 90% target line. Level and change plots coverage now against change over the period. Trends over time shows the median and the middle half of countries. It needs the Coverage - National table.

Compare countries page

- All datasets: pick any table from the grouped list and see its data.

sections.heading: Reading the output
sections.text:
Key columns you will see:

Column | Meaning
country

,

iso3 | Country name and ISO3 code, always first
adminlevel_1

,

district | Area, when the table is subnational
year | Reporting year
cov_penta3

,

cov_measles1

, ... | Facility coverage; the same name in every country, whichever denominator the country chose

Coverage indicators are ANC 1st trimester, ANC4+, institutional delivery, C-section, HIV test, institutional live births, PNC within 48h, Penta1, Penta3, Measles 1 and 2, BCG, OPV1-3, syphilis test and IPT2-3 (Admin 1 excludes OPV). The Parameters table holds each country's performance threshold, k-factors, national estimates such as nmr and sbr, survey estimates, survey_year and the chosen denominators. For the meaning of scores, adjustments and denominators, see the framework.

Continue with Exporting results.

DataSuite welcome page with numbered interface elements

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.text: The Countdown methodology is the analysis itself: each step, how it is done and how to read the results.

sections.heading: Reference

sections.heading: Privacy
